source.title: MetaOthello: A Controlled Study of Multiple World Models in Transformers
source.authors: Avi Chawla; Galen Hall; Juniper Lisa Lovato

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests representation alignment and interchangeability in controlled variants using probe-weight similarity, Procrustes alignment, and cross-probe interventions. These methods bear on the claim but are not a direct replication of the original studies’ overall convergence claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on a single 8-layer, dmodel=512 architecture trained on controlled game data. Results cited from prior work are not included as rows. Appendix layer-by-layer tables and plots contain extensive probe-accuracy values; the rows below retain the text-described findings and key comparisons relevant to the claim.
record.test_reason: Every comparison is within one trained model: probes for two game variants on the same 8-layer GPT's residual stream. The study never compares the representations of separately trained models, across seeds, architectures, scales or modalities. That cross-game, within-model sharing is a related but different construct from cross-model convergence. PRH is cited in related work and used as a section-title framing ('Platonic' board geometry), but no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that transformers trained on mixed Othello variants share a board-state representation across games, identical up to a rotation for token-scrambled variants. Conflicts are handled by a localized, steerable circuit (layer-4 MLP → layer-5 head 5 → layer-5 MLP), and the arbitration regime depends on how far the rule systems diverge.
record.recipe_differences: Uses controlled synthetic Othello variants, linear board-state probes, cosine similarity, orthogonal Procrustes alignment, and causal probe/activation interventions. It does not reproduce the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis’s broad cross-model scale and modality analysis, nor the original cross-seed convergence setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity depends strongly on whether orthogonal Procrustes alignment is applied (notably Classic–Iago). Activation-rotation performance also depends on intervention layer, with layer 8 degrading over longer prefixes. Representational dissimilarity varies with tile-level rule-conflict probability; arbitration differs between Classic–NoMidFlip and Classic–DelFlank regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Within one transformer trained on mixed game variants, linear board-state probes for different games are highly aligned (raw cosine ≈0.95 NoMidFlip; >0.90 DelFlank after Procrustes) and causally interchangeable: cross-probe steering error ≈ matched-probe error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single model trained on multiple related generative processes reuses a shared state representation across them rather than partitioning into separate subspaces.

fits_no_version.finding: For token-permuted isomorphic games, raw probe similarity is at the random baseline (0.03) but reaches 0.98 after an orthogonal rotation. A single global rotation applied at layers 1–7 restores near-baseline Iago performance; at layer 8 performance decays with move number.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model representations of isomorphic tasks with different surface vocabularies are equivalent up to an orthogonal rotation; raw cosine can miss this equivalence.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-game representational dissimilarity per tile tracks the probability that the games conflict on that tile (R²=0.95 at layer 8). For an effectively out-of-distribution variant, the alternative board representation degrades (67% vs 99%) and is partly restored by early-layer steering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared representations diverge in proportion to task conflict, localized to specific layers and circuits.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The evidence is from synthetic toy games and one 8-layer, dmodel=512 architecture; only 50/50 pairwise mixtures are tested. Models and probes use one fixed random seed and each model is trained once. The study does not test scale or cross-modal convergence. The main alignment analyses use linear probes, and some detailed layerwise evidence is presented in figures or appendix tables.
record.rows_left_out: Did not transcribe the complete per-layer and per-tile probe-accuracy arrays in Appendix Figure 12, or every plotted move-number value in Figures 4, 5, and 7. Those detailed values are not needed to capture the text-described alignment, transfer, and input-regime findings represented in the retained rows.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models; no scale or capability sweep (one 8-layer architecture).
No vision or language models, no paired image–caption data.
Single fixed seed (42); each model trained once; no cross-seed comparison.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations between two separately trained models; only within-model mappings between games.
No comparison of features or circuits across different models.
No cross-model similarity measured under varying metrics or inputs.
No cross-model alignment level, plateau, or shared-data explanation tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V4, V6 and V7, but every comparison is between probes or games inside a single model. None is between independently trained models, so no row matches the 'same kind of system' each version names. The 'Platonic' section title is framing only. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No model-scale sweep, capability comparison across scales, or comparison across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No vision-language models, paired images and captions, or cross-modal performance/alignment comparison.
Models and probes use one fixed random seed; the study does not compare independently initialized models or shared subspaces across seeds.

Tests transfer and orthogonal mappings in controlled Othello variants, not stitching layers, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or broad transfer between independently trained foundation models.
Does not test recurrence of the same interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits across different models.

Tests raw cosine versus Procrustes alignment and reports input-regime dependence in controlled games; does not systematically sweep similarity-measure settings such as neighbour counts or evaluate broad out-of-distribution datasets.

Shows shared structure alongside localized divergence under conflicting game rules, but does not compare shared versus different training data or objectives as causal explanations, test a common model of reality, or examine scaling/plateauing.

rows.subject: Classic-NoMidFlip mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Measured raw cosine similarity between corresponding board-state probe weights for the two variants.
rows.measure: Mean raw cosine similarity of probe weights
rows.baseline: Random-probe raw similarity shown in Figure 2; exact value not stated for this pair
rows.uncertainty: 95% CIs across 192 probe dimensions are shown; exact interval not stated
rows.note: The text describes high raw similarity in early and later layers.
rows.check: Within-model cross-game probe similarity, not alignment between independently trained models; does not bear on V6 (no cross-model convergence measurement).

rows.subject: Classic-NoMidFlip mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Applied per-layer orthogonal Procrustes alignment to corresponding board-state probe weights and measured cosine similarity.
rows.baseline: Raw similarity ≈0.95; random aligned baseline is shown in Figure 2
rows.value: Procrustes alignment yields only modest further improvement (≲0.05)
rows.uncertainty: 95% CIs across 192 probe dimensions are shown; exact interval not stated
rows.note: The paper says the alignment adds little where the raw correspondence is already high.
rows.check: Same model, two games' probes; not a mapping between models (V4) nor cross-model convergence (V6/V7).

rows.subject: Classic-Iago mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Measured raw cosine similarity between corresponding board-state probe weights for the two tokenization-isomorphic variants.
rows.measure: Raw cosine similarity of probe weights
rows.value: ≈0.03; described as indistinguishable from the random baseline
rows.uncertainty: 95% CIs across 192 probe dimensions are shown; exact interval not stated
rows.note: This low raw similarity contrasts with the result after rotational alignment.
rows.check: Raw similarity equals the random baseline (0.03), so as an alignment measure the state is absent, not observed. It is a within-model comparison either way.

rows.subject: Classic-Iago mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Applied per-layer orthogonal Procrustes alignment to corresponding board-state probe weights and measured cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of probe weights after alignment
rows.uncertainty: 95% CIs across 192 probe dimensions are shown; exact interval not stated
rows.note: The text interprets the result as the same latent structure up to a rotation induced by the input vocabularies.
rows.check: Within-model rotation equivalence between token vocabularies; not two models.

rows.subject: Classic-NoMidFlip mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Added a probe vector trained on one variant’s board state to activations across all layers, then measured predicted board-state error on the other variant.
rows.measure: Prediction error for the steered board state
rows.value: Cross-probe error ≈0.2 in Figure 3; described as nearly as effective as the correct probe
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI shown in Figure 3; exact interval not stated
rows.note: The matched correct-probe intervention is also ≈0.2 in Figure 3.
rows.check: Cross-probe steering within one model; not cross-model interchangeability.

rows.value: High at the first prediction, then decays with move number; no single numeric value stated

rows.subject: Classic-NoMidFlip mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Related tile-level representational dissimilarity to the probability that the two games assign different states to a tile on an ambiguous sequence.
rows.measure: R² between representational dissimilarity and conflict probability
rows.value: R² = 0.95 at layer 8; the text also reports a sharp increase after layer 5, from R²=0.35 at layer 5 to R²=0.73 at layer 6
rows.note: The result indicates that alignment/dissimilarity depends on whether the games conflict about the input state.
rows.check: Tile-level cross-game dissimilarity tracking conflict probability; about multi-task arbitration within a model, not convergence between models or input dependence of cross-model similarity.

rows.subject: Classic-DelFlank mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated DelFlank board-state probes on sequences in the Classic–DelFlank intersection where the authors say the model has selected the Classic world model.
rows.baseline: ≈99% for Classic probes on the same inputs
rows.value: ≈67% (reported more precisely as 67.1% in the intervention comparison)
rows.note: The paper contrasts this with high DelFlank-probe fidelity on random DelFlank games and interprets it as degradation of the alternative representation on these intersection inputs.
rows.check: Probe accuracy on intersection sequences; measures world-model selection, not representational convergence.

rows.subject: Classic-DelFlank mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Added a DelFlank-minus-Classic game-identity steering vector at early layers and measured downstream DelFlank board-probe accuracy.
rows.note: The intervention improves but does not restore the reported accuracy to the ≈99% Classic-probe result on the same inputs.
rows.check: Game-identity steering effect on probe accuracy; not a convergence measure.

rows.subject: Classic-DelFlank mixed model
rows.operation_detail: Added a DelFlank-minus-Classic game-identity steering vector at early layers and measured downstream DelFlank board-probe accuracy.
rows.note: The intervention improves but does not restore the reported accuracy to the ≈99% Classic-probe result on the same inputs.
rows.check: As R19.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Probe-weight comparisons across the tested rule and token variants
reader_labels.reason: Cross-probe interventions transfer across rule variants, and orthogonal alignment produces high probe similarity for DelFlank and Iago; see R2, R4, R6, R7, and R8.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Global activation rotation applied at layer 8
reader_labels.reason: The mapped Iago performance is initially high but decays with longer prefixes when the rotation is applied only at the final layer; see R16.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Raw cosine versus orthogonally aligned similarity, and ambiguous inputs with different rule-conflict probabilities
reader_labels.reason: The Iago raw cosine is at the random baseline while aligned similarity is 0.98, and the Classic–NoMidFlip representational relationship varies with conflict probability; see R5, R6, and R17.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Controlled mixed-game settings where variants conflict on board states
